svg.aria-label: Document indexing as a pipeline. After an upload or delete the control plane makes one HTTP call to the tenant’s chatbot backend, which loads every document under the prefix, extracts text, splits it into overlapping 200-word chunks, embeds each chunk as 384 values, upserts the vectors into the vector store and purges those of deleted files. Beneath, one 1,000-word PDF becomes seven chunks, seven vectors and seven rows.

g.text: the tenant’s own chatbot backend and storage
illustrative: a 1,000-word PDF uploaded to tenant “acme”
no credential and no file content
error or timeout: a stale-index warning
request held open while the resync runs
S3 bucket or Blob container, private
the chatbot may list and read, never write
Every call re-indexes every document under
the prefix: cost grows with document count.
One resync at a time, one more may wait;
any further call is answered 202 at once.
or Pinecone, the customer’s own index:
vectors and chunk text leave the account
If handbook.pdf is later deleted, step 6 of the next run removes all seven rows.
